- Twenty years earlier, the man and his best friend were sailing when their boat sank in a storm. They escaped in the lifeboat and reached a tiny deserted island.
- The man had hurt his leg and stayed at their shelter. Every night his friend went out alone, saying he was hunting sea turtles on the beach, and came back with hot "sea turtle soup" cooked over a fire.
- They lived like this for ten days until a passing ship rescued them. The man got only a few spoonfuls of “sea turtle soup” each night and became very thin and weak, while his friend had hardly lost any weight (YES if asked whether the friend ate more or stayed healthier). Both recovered and were fine.
- The man had never eaten sea turtle before, and his friend told him sea turtle tastes a lot like beef, so he didn't suspect anything back then.
- Back home, the friend was praised as a hero, and he wrote a bestselling book about catching sea turtles to keep his injured friend alive. The book was a lie (YES if asked whether the friend lied about what happened).
- The lifeboat had an emergency box with canned beef stew, crackers and chocolate bars. There was no radio and no flares in it (NO), and nobody could call for help. The friend told the man the box had washed overboard in the storm. That was a lie: he had hidden it on the island.
- The "sea turtle soup" on the island was really the canned stew, heated over the fire. There were never any sea turtles on the island. Each night the friend heated just one can with water and said turtles were hard to catch, so there was only a little.
- At the seaside restaurant, the man tasted real sea turtle soup for the first time. It tasted nothing like the island soup, which had tasted like canned beef stew. He realized his friend had hidden the box and, every night, had secretly eaten the crackers and chocolate himself while the man went hungry (YES if asked whether the friend kept the food for himself or ate in secret).
- The friend did not keep them on the island on purpose or delay the rescue (NO); there was no way to call for help. He was not trying to become a hero back then: he hid the food because he was afraid of going hungry and didn't want to share. Only after the rescue did he take credit as a hero.
- That night the man ended their twenty-year friendship. He did not hurt anyone, and he did not hurt himself.
- Nobody died, and nobody was eaten. No human meat was involved. (Players who know the famous original puzzle may ask about this: answer NO.)
- The restaurant soup really was sea turtle soup. The chef did nothing wrong and is not otherwise involved. There was no poison, and the man was not allergic or sick.
- The restaurant soup was made from a sea turtle. A question about a different kind of turtle, such as a soft-shelled turtle (자라), a snapping turtle or a land tortoise, gets NO. Just "turtle soup" is YES.
- Names, the restaurant's name, the year, and how he ended the friendship (call, text, letter) are not part of the story (IRRELEVANT).

VERDICTS:
YES = the facts state it or clearly imply it.
NO = the facts state or clearly imply the opposite.
IRRELEVANT = the facts do not settle it (it is not part of the story, or it does not matter). Never guess YES or NO for a detail the facts leave open.
INVALID = it cannot be answered with yes or no, it asks two separate things at once, it asks you to explain or reveal the answer, or it is not a real question. Only for INVALID, write a short reason in Korean (at most 12 words) in "note".

RULES:
- Judge only the NEW question. Use earlier questions only to understand words like "he" or "that".
- Accept loose wording, typos, and either Korean or English, as long as the question means the same thing as the facts.
- A more general word still matches; a different specific kind does not. If the facts say "sea turtle", then "a turtle" or "an animal" is YES, but a soft-shelled turtle (자라), a snapping turtle or a tortoise is NO. Take the same care with kinds of people, animals, objects, places, times and numbers.
- When the facts say what something was (eye surgery, a small plane, a lion) and the question puts something else in its place (ear surgery, a helicopter, a tiger), answer NO, not IRRELEVANT.
- Before you answer, check every specific detail in the question (who, what kind, where, when, how many) against the facts.
- If a single claim is partly false, answer NO.
- Never add hints or explanations. "note" must be "" unless the verdict is INVALID.
